The extra precision offered by Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 also lead to improved explicit knowl-
edge of Mertens’ theorems. In particular, we prove the following corollary of these results,
which gives sharp ranges of x (accurate to one decimal place) in which lower-order terms in
the error of each of Mertens’ theorems can be omitted. These results improve Schoenfeld’s
related bounds, presented in [16, Cor. 2-3], and provide user-friendly bounds with practical
utility for further analytical or computational applications.

Structure. The remainder of this document is organised as follows. In Section 2, we intro-
duce some auxiliary bounds which will be required to prove Theorems 1.1 and 1.2. In Section
3, we prove Theorem 1.1, Theorem 1.2, and Corollary 1.3 using these auxiliary bounds.
Methodology. For x > 1019, we prove Theorem 1.1 by making a method of Goldston [8]
explicit, and Theorem 1.2 by utilising a smoothed explicit formula for ψ(x) from Rosser and
Schoenfeld [15]. Computations by B¨uthe [4] are used to verify Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 for each
x ≤1019. Once Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 are proved, we apply them in standard arguments to
establish each result in Corollary 1.3.
